known_risks: the test set is libpostal's vendor evaluation set; Senzing may have tuned on it, so libpostal plays at home
the gold labels follow libpostal's label scheme (e.g. 'house' for venue names, 'city_district'), which arche does not model; those fields are not scored
arche never produces unit, so any gold unit is a miss for arche
GB (255), AU (76) and ZA (53) are small; intervals will be wide
no African country but ZA; G0b covers NG, GH, KE
question: Given the address span, how often do arche's parser and libpostal (Senzing v1.2 model) split it into the right components, by country?

arms.arche: arche.addr.parse.parse_address on the whole string; None = every field empty; house_number = street_number, else plot without the word 'Plot'; suburb = neighborhood, else area; state = region; unit is never produced
arms.libpostal: postal.parser.parse_address with Senzing's v1.2 address_parser model and v1.1 language classifier and data files; repeated labels joined with a space

rule.comparison: paired bootstrap of libpostal minus arche parse_correct (10,000 resamples, seed 0, unit address); verdict per country: libpostal if the 95% interval is above 0, arche if below 0, else no_difference
rule.decision: libpostal becomes the default parser for a country only where the verdict is libpostal; elsewhere arche's parser stays default
rule.interim: an arche-only run before libpostal is built is allowed and reported as interim; the verdict comes only from a run with both arms
rule.match: equal after casefold and removing every non-alphanumeric character; a field empty in the gold must be empty in the prediction
rule.population: rows of test_data.csv whose country_code is us, gb, au or za
rule.primary: parse_correct: every field matches; rate with Wilson 95% interval, per country (us, gb, au, za) and over all four
secondary: per field recall and spurious counts
country inference is not scored here

test.source: Senzing libpostal-data files/tests/v1.2.0/test_data.csv (Apache-2.0), read from ~/shannon/oss/libpostal-data; not copied into this repo

why: The place-text plan (docs, 22 Nov, rev 2) makes libpostal the one optional parser backend; G0 decides per country whether it earns that place. Senzing's own v1.1-vs-v1.2 comparison reports parse failure US 4.6%, AU 1.3%, GB 22.9%, ZA 34%, and holds no NG, GH or KE addresses
